title: Pink Clouding: What's New in Taylor Swift's Latest Song
seoTitle: Pink Clouding: What's New in Taylor Swift's Latest Song
subtitle: The track has fans speculating about who the lyrics are targeting
excerpt: Taylor Swift released "Pink Clouding" on the expanded version of her 15th album, fueling speculation about the identity of the person mentioned in the lyrics.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Last Thursday, September 25, Taylor Swift released four unreleased tracks on an expanded edition of her 15th studio album. Among them, “Pink Clouding” caught fans' attention and sparked an intense debate about the song's subject.

What is "pink clouding"?

According to Healthline, the term describes a phase of addiction recovery marked by euphoria and excitement. Dictionary.com adds that this feeling of euphoria is often followed by a crash when reality returns. In the song, Swift references this concept by singing that she was “pink clouding from the thrill of it”.

Who might be at the center of the song?

Some fans point to former partner Tom Hiddleston, with whom the singer had a three-month romance in 2016. The lyrics mention that the relationship ended “amicably” and that Swift “didn’t want to leave the guy empty-handed.” On September 25, the singer herself sang in the chorus: “I didn’t want to let you down” and “So I left you up there on a pink cloud”.

Comparisons with other relationships

Besides Hiddleston, the fan community also suggested that the song could refer to Taylor Lautner, another of Swift's ex-partners. However, the text does not confirm any of these hypotheses.

The context of the new track

“Pink Clouding” appears on an album that also features “Patient Zero,” “Cleveland!,” and “Babylon.” The track's lyrics describe a situation where the narrator realizes she was in a “cursed time” when getting involved with someone after a breakup. She acknowledges that, although she promised something, she ended up leaving the other person with a “scar” and “didn’t deserve” the treatment she received.

Fan reaction

On X, Swift's followers began discussing who the song could be targeting. The reference to Hiddleston was the most cited, but the lyrics themselves leave room for multiple interpretations.

With information from Yahoo, Just Jared, AOL.com.
